security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline option names, and sibling documentation links. No prompt injection, credential access, or hidden data-exfiltration instructions were found in the reviewed skill file. A separate semantic concern remains because the skill allows runtime execution through npx firecrawl.

remediation.suggestion: Prefer the installed firecrawl CLI, or pin npx use to a reviewed Firecrawl package version before allowing marketplace publication.

remediation.issue: User-controlled CLI arguments and file paths
remediation.suggestion: Document that user text, URLs, schemas, and output paths must be quoted and kept within the intended .firecrawl workspace directory.

content.user_title: Extract Website Data with Firecrawl Agent
content.value_statement: Complex websites often require multi-page navigation before data can be collected. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to run Firecrawl Agent and return structured website data.
actual_capabilities: Runs Firecrawl Agent for autonomous multi-page website extraction.
Starts extraction from one or more target URLs.
Uses inline or file-based schemas for structured output.
Waits for agent jobs and returns results inline.
Saves extraction output to a local file path.
Caps agent credit use with a maximum credit setting.
limitations: Requires Firecrawl CLI or npx access and available Firecrawl credits.
Results depend on site accessibility, page structure, and Firecrawl Agent performance.
Multi-page agent runs can take several minutes and consume more credits.
Does not replace authorization checks for private, paywalled, or restricted data.

use_cases.title: SaaS Pricing Research
use_cases.description: Collect plan names, prices, feature limits, and source URLs from complex pricing pages.

use_cases.title: Catalog Monitoring
use_cases.description: Extract product names, prices, availability, and links from category pages that require navigation.

use_cases.title: Directory Data Collection
use_cases.description: Build structured lists of organizations, locations, categories, and profile links from public directories.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Pricing Extraction
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Firecrawl Agent to extract pricing tiers from [site URL]. Wait for completion and save the structured result under .firecrawl/pricing.json.

prompt_templates.title: Product Catalog Extraction
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract product names, prices, availability, and product URLs from [catalog URL]. Use a schema and return only verified fields.

prompt_templates.title: Directory Extraction with Limits
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract organization names, categories, locations, contact pages, and source URLs from [directory URL]. Set a credit limit of [number].

prompt_templates.title: Schema File Extraction Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my workspace schema file at [path] to extract nested plan, feature, and limitation data from [site URL]. Save results under .firecrawl.

output_examples.input: Extract pricing from a SaaS pricing page.
output_examples.output: A structured pricing summary with plan names, monthly prices, annual discounts, feature limits, and source URLs.

output_examples.input: Get products from an ecommerce category.
output_examples.output: A product table covering item name, price, availability, product link, and fields that could not be verified.

output_examples.input: Collect directory entries from multiple starting pages.
output_examples.output: A deduplicated list of directory records with organization names, categories, locations, profile links, and source pages.

best_practices: Keep output files inside a dedicated .firecrawl directory.
Use schemas when you need predictable fields and easier validation.
Set credit limits before running broad or uncertain extractions.
anti_patterns: Do not use the agent for a single simple page when a scrape is enough.
Do not extract private, paywalled, or restricted data without authorization.
Do not pass unreviewed shell text, unsafe paths, or secret values into commands.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It guides Firecrawl Agent to navigate websites and extract structured data for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it scrape pages directly inside the model?
faq.answer: No. It guides an approved Firecrawl CLI command, and Firecrawl performs the navigation and extraction.

faq.question: When should I use it instead of simple scraping?
faq.answer: Use it when the target data spans multiple pages or requires the agent to discover where the data appears.

faq.question: Can it use a schema?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports inline schemas and schema files for predictable structured output.

faq.question: Where are results saved?
faq.answer: The examples save results under .firecrawl, and users should keep outputs in that workspace area.

faq.question: What should I check before running it?
faq.answer: Confirm authorization for the target site, set a credit limit, and review paths before saving output.
